componentPlan.focusQuote: Some hazards, such as lahars and landslides, can occur even when a volcano is not erupting.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Shows hazard locations on a volcano sketch before classifying each hazard type.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Volcanoes produce a wide variety of hazards that can kill people and destroy property.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Groups eruption products, flows and lahars by their defining characteristics.

overview.headline: Volcano hazards that threaten lives, property and climate

keyPoints.point: Students learn that large explosive eruptions can endanger distant people and affect global climate.
keyPoints.quote: Large explosive eruptions can endanger people and property hundreds of miles away and even affect global climate.

keyPoints.point: Students learn how eruption columns grow rapidly and form clouds that threaten aircraft.
keyPoints.quote: Eruption columns can grow rapidly and reach more than 12 miles above a volcano in less than 30 minutes, forming an eruption cloud.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that pyroclastic flows are extremely hot and move fast enough to destroy everything in their path.
keyPoints.quote: These pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that lahars are mud and water flows that can occur even when a volcano is quiet.
keyPoints.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

keyTerms.gloss: Solid and molten rock fragments blasted from an eruption
keyTerms.quote: An explosive eruption blasts solid and molten rock fragments (tephra) and volcanic gases into the air with tremendous force.

keyTerms.gloss: Molten rock that pours onto the surface to form flows
keyTerms.quote: Molten rock (magma) that pours or oozes onto the Earth’s surface is called lava and forms lava flows.

keyTerms.gloss: Flows of mud and volcanic debris that rush down valleys
keyTerms.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

keyTerms.gloss: Small openings where gases reach the surface
keyTerms.quote: Even when a volcano is not erupting, cracks in the ground allow gases to reach the surface through small openings called fumaroles.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains major volcano hazards including eruption columns, gases, lava flows, pyroclastic flows, landslides and lahars, plus monitoring for public warning.
